body: Large language model (LLM) assistants increasingly help users draft content for third-party recipients. During private drafting, the user or the model may introduce an item and later remove or replace it. The model may remove the item from the intended content but reveal it again when stating the edit. We call such statements revision traces. For example, after a user removes the password before sharing a configuration file, the model may delete it but leave a comment saying, "Removed the password 'No****4!' as requested." A third-party recipient who sees only the delivered file can therefore recover the withdrawn password from the comment. In an in-the-wild analysis of three public conversation corpora, we identify 26,753 revision requests, of which 2,363 (8.8%) leave revision traces. We study them in greater depth under controlled conditions by introducing RevLeakBench, a benchmark of 100 tasks across five scenarios with a conversation track and an agent track. We measure trace occurrence, withdrawn-item recovery, trace position, and required-content retention. Across six models, about half of the deliverables in both tracks state the edit after a revocation, and a reader that sees only the deliverable can recover the withdrawn item from about 13% of them. Telling the model that its entire reply will be forwarded to the recipient still leaves revision traces in 36.4% of the deliverables. We compare prompt defenses and a delivery boundary, and propose an output-side filter that sharply reduces recovery with little loss of required content. We believe our work can benefit efforts to understand and mitigate unintended disclosure in LLM interactions.
summaryZh: 本文探讨了LLM在辅助用户编辑内容时，通过“修订痕迹”无意泄露敏感信息的安全隐患。研究发现，模型在删除敏感信息后，往往会在回复中提及删除操作，导致第三方接收者可从修订记录中恢复原始数据。作者提出了RevLeakBench基准测试，评估了六种主流模型，发现约半数模型存在此类泄露。研究建议通过输出端过滤机制来有效缓解该风险，为提升LLM交互的安全性提供了实证依据。

glossary.explanationZh: 模型在编辑或修改内容时，在输出中留下的关于修改过程的描述性文本。
文中提出的用于评估LLM修订痕迹泄露风险的基准测试集。
指模型在生成过程中无意中泄露了用户本意想要隐藏的敏感信息。
一种部署在模型输出端的过滤机制，用于拦截包含敏感修订痕迹的回复。
